meta.title: Sonos · Commercial Command Center
meta.subtitle: A quarter of continuous collection, extrapolated from the measured snapshot
meta.subject: local-yeti

disclosure.headline: The figures on these screens are extrapolated, not measured.
disclosure.body: Every Sonos lane we hold today is a single capture. This dashboard answers what a quarter of continuous collection would look like: the measured snapshot is used as an anchor and a 13-week daily panel is simulated around it, with retail-calendar seasonality, promotional cycles, stock episodes and competitive response. Levels are pinned to what was measured; shapes are modelled. Nothing here should be read as a reported result.

anchors.measured: Street price, list price, discount rate and offer count for 15 Amazon listings across 5 brands, monthly 2025-10 to 2026-03
anchors.pins: Every daily price ladder is bounded by its brand's measured discount rate — Sonos 0.1%, Amazon Echo 9%, Apple HomePod 43.3%, Bose 7.5%, JBL 31.4%.

anchors.measured: PDP shelf price for 9 models across 5 retailers, captured 2026-08-13
anchors.pins: Each simulated ladder is scaled to land on the captured price at the capture date.

anchors.measured: 71 promotion verbatims across 28 product pages, each located and outlined in the captured image
anchors.pins: The mechanic set, the per-retailer mix, and every promotion type shown.
Carried and not-carried cells are held fixed; only 'not readable' cells are extrapolated.

anchors.measured: Share of days in the last audited month with a buyable Amazon offer — Sonos 62%, Amazon Echo 100%, Apple HomePod 67%, Bose 67%, JBL 100%
anchors.pins: The target in-stock rate each simulated episode series is drawn against.

anchors.measured: 84 delivery-promise readings across 9 models, 5 retailers and 6 cities
anchors.pins: Week-one lead time for every model-retailer-city triple that was captured.

anchors.measured: Share of the result grid per retailer per search term across 3 terms, 3 passes
anchors.pins: The level each daily shelf-share series reverts to.

anchors.measured: Share of the AI answer across 3 engines by funnel stage. Any engine shown on the dashboard beyond those is modelled off their mean and is a column of illustration, not a measurement.
anchors.pins: The per-engine and per-stage level each daily series reverts to, for the engines that were captured.

anchors.measured: Amazon star rating weighted by rating count, and monthly aspect scores from captured reviews across 8 aspects
anchors.pins: Rating levels, and every aspect month that had a real reading is passed through untouched.

anchors.measured: NOTHING. No traffic capture is present in this checkout.
anchors.pins: Levels sized to the order of magnitude a panel reports for these domains, and shaped by the same events as every other lane. Illustrative of the measure, not of the brand.

disclosure.paletteNote: Sonos’s own black fails the chroma and lightness checks for a categorical slot and reads as “no data”, and Amazon teal against Apple blue fails colour-vision separation.

overview.text: Over the 13 weeks Sonos holds 38.4% of the AI answer — first of the 5 — against 1.3% of the retail shelf, fourth of the 5. The brand is being recommended far more often than it is being seen on a result grid.
Price discipline is intact: Sonos transacts at 95.6% of MSRP, first of the 5, while the set as a whole runs at 86.9%.
Share of category traffic sits at 16%, fourth of the 5, and moved -0.2pp between the open and the close of the quarter.
In-stock rate of 59.4% is last of the 5; 375 separate out-of-stock episodes cost 1011 listing-days across the carried estate.

traffic.text: No traffic capture for this brand's domain — the level here is sized, not measured.
Sonos takes 16% of the tracked brand-site visits, fourth of the 5; Amazon Echo is the nearest of the rest on 33.3%.
Assistant referrals grew from 8.3k to 16.7k sessions a day across the quarter — a 102.1% rise, the fastest-growing channel in the mix.
Paid search carries 12% of Sonos sessions, the third-least paid-dependent of the 5; JBL runs the most paid-dependent mix at 24.1%.

ai.text: Sonos is first of the 5 on share of the AI answer at 38.4%.
Presence is uneven by engine: ChatGPT returns Sonos in 43.4% of answers against 35.2% on Perplexity — a 8.2-point spread on the same prompt set.
The strongest funnel position is evaluation at 46.8%, the weakest consideration at 30.6%.

shelf.text: Shelf share of 1.3% puts Sonos fourth of the 5; Bose is the nearest of the rest on 12.7%.
Presence concentrates where the intent is specific — "multiroom speaker" returns Sonos in 2.9% of the grid, against 0.7% on the weakest term.
3% of Sonos shelf presence is paid — the second-least paid-reliant of the 5. JBL buys its way onto the grid at 36.7%, which is why Sonos share moves against it in event weeks.
Target reads thinnest for Sonos at 0% of the grid, against 5.4% at Amazon — a 5.4-point gap between the brand's best and worst shelf.

distribution.text: Sonos occupies 28 of 35 possible model-by-retailer cells — 74.8% weighted for the days each listing was actually live, fourth of the 5.
8 listings changed state inside the quarter: 0 dropped, 5 appeared, 3 lapsed and returned.
Buy-box ownership averages 90% on the marketplaces, second of the 5 — every point lost is a sale credited to a reseller at a price the brand did not set.

availability.text: In-stock rate of 59.4% is last of the 5; 375 out-of-stock episodes cost 1011 listing-days over the quarter.
None of the 375 episodes followed a deep discount, so these are replenishment gaps rather than promotions outrunning supply. The longest ran 5 days on Era 100 at Amazon, from 2026-06-12.

delivery.text: The Sonos delivery promise averages 5.1 days — the slowest of the 5, against 3.8 days for Amazon Echo, the fastest of the rest.
The promise is not national: Denver, CO waits 5.7 days against 4.4 in New York, NY — a 1.3-day spread on the same catalogue.

pricing.text: Sonos realises 95.6% of MSRP across the quarter, first of the 5 — the category runs 86.9% and JBL clears at 76.1%.
Arc Ultra carries the widest cross-retailer spread at $46.26 on average and $81.08 at its widest — a shopper comparing two tabs sees two different brands.
3 listings traded below the 86% floor for 22 days in total, worst at 1.6% under.

promotions.text: Sonos runs a price promotion on 10.1% of carried listing-days — the least promoted of the 5. JBL is on promotion 26.5% of the time.
When Sonos does promote it goes 4.5% deep against a category mean of 14.7% — the shallowest of the 5 on discount depth.
60% of Sonos price events open inside a retail-calendar window, spread across 5 retailers; 50 episodic events ran in the quarter at a mean 8.3 days each.
The mechanic doing most of the work is delivery offer at 31.7% of Sonos promotional days.

tco.text: Attach-weighted, the shelf price understates what a Sonos buyer actually pays by 0.3% — the narrowest of the 5. Apple HomePod shows a 2.3% gap, 7.5x wider, so a shelf-price comparison against it is not a like-for-like read.
Move 2 at Newegg carries the widest single gap: $444.18 on the shelf against $434.25 attach-weighted, of which $9.61 is funded by the brand rather than the retailer.

15 of 28 Sonos listings carry three or more simultaneous mechanics. The more mechanics on a page, the less the shelf price says about the transaction — and the harder a competitor's headline price is to read straight.

voice.text: Sonos rates 4.62★, second of the 5; JBL leads on 4.8★.
Review velocity of 3.5k over the quarter is fourth of the 5 — a smaller base to defend the rating with.
